action: Place probe at the distal posterior ankle (the bottom). Locate the calcaneal bone. Visualize the insertion point of the tendon.
interpretation: Identify the calcaneal bone as a 'bright white line casting a shadow.' Confirm the Achilles tendon is attached to this bony landmark.

action: Optimize depth and focus for near-field imaging.
interpretation: Note that the tendon is an 'extremely superficial structure,' requiring appropriate parameter settings.

action: Anchor the scanning hand by placing the pinky finger over the Achilles tendon. Slide the probe proximally to follow the tendon's length up to the musculotendinous junction.
interpretation: Trace the continuous length of the tendon from the calcaneus to the point where muscle fibers begin.

action: Inspect the tissue integrity while scanning.
interpretation: Check for rupture; if present, the 'longitudinal fibers will be interrupted by an area of blackness or echolucency.'

action: Upon reaching the musculotendinous junction, rotate the probe 90 degrees into a transverse orientation. Slide the probe distally to follow the tendon down.
interpretation: Establish a transverse view of the tendon and track it distally.
Examine the cross-section for any deformities within the fibers that make up the Achilles tendon.
This marks the conclusion of the ultrasonographic exam of the Achilles tendon.
